subject: ParkView go-live: cutover checklist and SDK retry policy
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@parkviewhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@parkviewhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: ParkView go-live: cutover and SDK migration questions

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We need a concise go-live playbook for our engineers so we can migrate our app from the legacy hosted endpoint to Redwood's dedicated endpoint with minimal user disruption. High-level asks:

- A short SDK setup (Node/Python) and sample call we can drop into our service.
- Recommended timeouts and retry/backoff strategy (we have bursty traffic during patient portal peak).
- Any required network config (IP allowlist, TLS/certs, DNS cutover advice).
- Can Redwood honor a short grace period where both endpoints are live so we can shift traffic gradually?

Attached is our internal onboarding checklist and a note on compliance needs. Can your implementation lead share a one-page cutover checklist by end of week?

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Director, Platform Engineering
ParkView Health

[Attachment: parkview_onboarding-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@parkviewhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: ParkView go-live: cutover checklist and SDK retry policy

Elena / team —

I'll own the implementation runway. Proposed schedule and owners:

- Thurs 2/12 (10:00 PT): Pre-cutover sync (network, infra, SSO) — Monica (CS), Jonas (SE), ParkView Ops
- Mon 2/16: Run smoke tests on staging (ParkView) — ParkView Eng
- Tue 2/17: Cutover window (ParkView peak hours avoided; earliest 02:00–05:00 local) — Monica + on-call

Notes & operational guidance:
- For burst protection, enable client-side token bucket limiter (rate ~ 100rps per instance) and use server-side quota to shape traffic.
- Use request_id headers for tracing (X-Request-ID) so we can correlate traces in our console.
- We'll open a short-lived SRE channel in Slack for the cutover; request a point person.

I pulled together a drafted MOU for implementation ownership — attaching. Please review and sign so we can lock dates.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: parkview-moa.docx (docx)]

From: Elena Torres <elena@parkviewhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@parkviewhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 14:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: ParkView go-live: cutover checklist and SDK retry policy

Monica / Jonas —

Thanks, schedule looks good. Quick clarification from our SRE: during the warm-up window, if we see a sustained stream of 429s from Redwood for a particular tenant key, will Redwood provide an alternate lower-capacity model endpoint automatically, or do we need to implement a manual fallback? Also, can you confirm if the SDK propagates Retry-After from 429 responses?

Example log excerpt from our pre-test (truncated):
[2026-02-12 03:11:22] request_id=abc123 status=429 model=redwood-xl tokens=321
[2026-02-12 03:11:23] request_id=abc124 status=429 model=redwood-xl tokens=33

We'd prefer an automatic fallback path so we don't have to ship feature toggles during cutover.

Best,
Elena

On Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 11:02 AM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Elena —
> 
> Appreciate the clear list. I put together a short cutover plan below...
> (full message quoted)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@parkviewhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 15:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: ParkView go-live: cutover checklist and SDK retry policy

Elena / Sanjay —

Short answers to the 429 questions and final action items before cutover:

- Automatic fallback: yes — during overload we can route traffic to a compatible "degraded" model variant (e.g., redwood-medium -> redwood-small) automatically for the tenant key. We'll enable this for ParkView during the 72-hour warm-up unless you prefer to opt-out. This is a routing policy we apply at the orchestration layer and is transparent to the SDK (it remains the same endpoint).
- Retry-After: our platform will surface Retry-After when applicable. SDKs do not automatically honor Retry-After in versions prior to v1.3 — we will push a small patch to the Node/Python SDKs used in your fleet to prefer Retry-After over computed backoff when present.

Final action items: 
1) ParkView signs the MOU (Doc attached/DocuSign link below) — Owner: Sanjay (by 2/18)
2) Redwood to enable routing fallback and provide CIDR block — Owner: Jonas (done by 2/16)
3) Joint smoke test on staging (2/16) — Owner: ParkView Eng
4) Cutover window (2/17, 02:00–05:00) — Owner: Monica (CS)

Operational contacts:
- Redwood on-call (cutover): se-cutover@redwood.ai
- Slack channel: #cutover-parkview (invites sent)

Link to signed SOW when ready: https://docusign.com/rw/SOW/PARK-0042
Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/parkview-onboarding-plan

I'll run the dry-run with your ops on Monday morning PT and deploy the SDK patch to our prerelease channel. Let me know if ParkView wants mTLS turned on for the dedicated endpoint — that adds ~1 business day for cert exchange.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth cutover.

— Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
